title: Read and draw graphs
goal: I can read a picture graph and use it to add and compare.

learn.intro: A picture graph uses pictures to show how many. The key tells what 1 picture means.

example.problem: The graph shows books borrowed in 1 week. How many more on Tuesday than on Thursday?
steps: Read the key. 1 picture is 1 book.
Tuesday has 7 books. Thursday has 2 books.
"How many more" asks for the gap. Subtract: 7 - 2 = 5. Check: 2 + 5 = 7.
example.answer: 5 more books are borrowed on Tuesday. 7 - 2 = 5.

howto.title: How to read a picture graph
steps: Read the title and the key.
Count the pictures in each row you need.
Add for "in all". Subtract for "how many more".

try.text: How many more shells does Ben have than Kumar? {b} shells
try.explanation: Ben has 5 shells. Kumar has 2 shells. 5 - 2 = 3. Check: 2 + 3 = 5.

items.text: Look at the graph. Fill in the blanks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: {b} children chose catch.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which game did the fewest children choose? {l}

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which 2 games got the same number of votes? {l}

items.explanation: Count the faces in each row. Catch has 5. Marbles has 3, the fewest. Skipping and tag both have 7.

items.text: Look at the graph in Question 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many more children chose skipping than hopscotch? {b} children

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many children are there altogether? {b} children

items.explanation: (a) "How many more" means subtract: 7 - 4 = 3. (b) Every child chose 1 game, so add every row: 7 + 7 + 5 + 4 + 3 = 26.

items.text: Look at the graph in Question 1. Circle True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.text: More children chose catch than hopscotch. {circ:True|False}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Marbles got 4 votes. {circ:True|False}

items.explanation: (a) Catch has 5 and hopscotch has 4, so it is true. (b) Marbles has 3 faces, not 4: false.

items.text: Siti asks 5 friends which game they like best. 4 friends choose tag. Is it true that most children in the school like tag best? {circ:Yes|No|We cannot tell}
items.explanation: Only 5 children were asked. Other children in the school may choose other games. So we cannot tell.

items.text: Look at the graph. Fill in the blanks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Who has the most stickers? {l}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ben has {b} stickers.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Mei has {b} more stickers than Siti.

items.explanation: Mei has 9 stars, the most. Ben has 3. Mei and Siti: 9 - 5 = 4.

items.text: Look at the graph in Question 5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many stickers do Ali and Ben have in all? {b} stickers

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ali gives 2 stickers to Ben. How many stickers does Ben have now? {b} stickers

items.text: Draw 1 face for each child. 7 children chose water, 4 chose milk and 2 chose tea. How many faces did you draw in all? {b} faces
items.explanation: Draw 7 faces for water, 4 for milk and 2 for tea. Count them all: 7 + 4 + 2 = 13.

items.text: Look at the graph. Fill in the blanks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: On which day were the most cookies sold? {l}

parts.label: b
parts.text: {b} cookies were sold on Thursday.

parts.label: c
parts.text: How many more cookies were sold on Friday than on Monday? {b} cookies

items.explanation: Wednesday has 8 cookies, the most. Thursday has 5. Friday 7 and Monday 4: 7 - 4 = 3.

items.text: Ali has 5 books. Mei has 3 more books than Ali. Draw Mei's row. How many books does Mei have? {b} books
items.explanation: "3 more than Ali" means add: 5 + 3 = 8. Draw 8 books in Mei's row.

items.text: Ravi makes 12 treats in all. 7 are cookies. The rest are cakes. Draw the cakes. How many cakes does Ravi make? {b} cakes
items.explanation: The rest is 12 - 7 = 5. Draw 5 pictures in the Cakes row. Check: 7 + 5 = 12.

items.text: Each face stands for 2 children. A half face stands for 1 child.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many children chose chess? {b} children

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many more children chose chess than singing? {b} children

items.hint: Count in 2s along each row. A half face is 1 more child.
items.explanation: Chess: 5 faces make 10 and the half face makes 11. Singing: 3 faces make 6. 11 - 6 = 5.

items.text: 30 children vote for a class trip. Zoo gets 9 votes, museum 6 and beach 8. The rest vote for the farm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many children chose the farm? {b} children

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which place got the most votes? {l}

items.hint: Add the 3 numbers you know. Then count on to 30.
items.explanation: 9 + 6 + 8 = 23. From 23 to 30 is 7, so 7 children chose the farm. Zoo has 9 votes, the most.

items.text: Look at the 2 graphs. Their keys are not the same.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Graph P shows {b} children. Graph Q shows {b} children.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which graph shows more children? {circ:Graph P|Graph Q}

items.hint: Do not count the pictures only. Read the key first.
items.explanation: Graph P has 6 faces and each is 1 child: 6 children. Graph Q has 2 faces and each is 5 children: 5 + 5 = 10. Graph Q has more children, even with fewer pictures.

items.text: Ravi, Lily, Jamie and Ray find 24 shells in all. Ravi finds 7. Lily finds 2 fewer than Ravi. Jamie and Ray find the same number.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Lily finds {b} shells.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Jamie finds {b} shells.

items.hint: Find Lily first. Then share what is left.
items.explanation: Lily: 7 - 2 = 5. Ravi and Lily have 7 + 5 = 12. The rest is 24 - 12 = 12. Jamie and Ray share it equally: 6 each. Check: 7 + 5 + 6 + 6 = 24.

items.text: A graph has rows for kites, balls and ropes. There are 18 toys. There are 2 more balls than kites. There is 1 more rope than kites.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Kites: {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Balls: {b}

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ropes: {b}

items.hint: Take away the extra balls and the extra rope. Share what is left between 3 rows.
items.explanation: The extra toys are 2 + 1 = 3. 18 - 3 = 15. Shared equally among 3 rows: 5 each. Kites 5, balls 5 + 2 = 7, ropes 5 + 1 = 6. Check: 5 + 7 + 6 = 18.

items.text: In Wei's graph, each picture stands for 2 stickers. Wei has 6 pictures. Siti has the same number of stickers as Wei. In Siti's graph, each picture stands for 3 stickers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many stickers does Wei have? {b} stickers

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many pictures does Siti draw? {b} pictures

items.hint: Count in 2s to find the stickers. Then count in 3s.
items.explanation: (a) 6 pictures of 2: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. (b) Count in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12. That is 4 pictures.

items.text: Use the graph for Questions 1 to 4. Kumar read {b} books.
items.explanation: Count the books in Kumar's row: 8.

items.text: How many more books did Kumar read than Aisha? {b} books
How many books did the 2 children read in all? {b} books
Who read the fewest books? {l}
items.explanation: Aisha read 3 books. Kumar read 8 books. 3 is fewer.
